source.title: Towards Robust Evaluation of Unlearning in LLMs via Data Transformations
source.authors: Abhinav Joshi; Shaswati Saha; Divyaksh Shukla; Sriram Vema; Harsh Jhamtani; Manas Gaur; Ashutosh Modi

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning results persist when the same fictitious facts are presented in different formats, and reports that performance varies by format. This challenges the adequacy of judging forgetting from the default Q&A format alone.
record.gate_note: Rows record step-30 results on the forget set from Tables 3 and 4. The default pretrained checkpoint is the reported reference; the table also reports the fine-tuned step-0 checkpoint, which is noted where useful. Odd-one-out measures distinguishing forget and retain items, not retrieval of forgotten facts, so those rows are linked to none of the claim versions. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The model is unlearned on TOFU in the default Q&A format, then the same forgotten facts are probed in other formats (MCQA, Cloze, analogy). That is a rephrasing probe of hidden knowledge (E). It also checks whether default-format forgetting coexists with kept retain knowledge (A). Results: at step 30, Cloze keeps forget-set knowledge that Q&A shows as removed. Llama2 KL: fully kept. Phi-1.5 (all methods) and Llama2 gradient diff: partly kept.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that forgetting judged only in the default Q&A format can be unreliable, since unlearned models differ by format (notably Cloze), and that benchmarks should test several formats. They also report that unlearning lowers comprehension performance even when the facts are given in context.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the TOFU setting and its gradient ascent, KL minimization, and gradient-difference methods, but evaluates transformed formats of the forget and retain information rather than only the default Q&A format.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation format changes the measured outcome. The study also reports results across three unlearning methods and multiple unlearning steps; step-30 values are extracted here.

fits_no_version.finding: Odd-one-out success stays near pretrained and 4-option chance (about 0.21–0.27) throughout unlearning, for both models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning does not make models distinguish forget-set from retain-set facts (membership-style probe).

fits_no_version.finding: With the answer supplied in context, unlearned models score lower on forget- and retain-set comprehension (e.g. Llama GA forget 0.2087, retain 0.2715 vs finetuned about 0.566).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based unlearning damages in-context reading comprehension, not only the targeted stored knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The experiments use two models and three unlearning methods on a fictitious-author benchmark. The excerpt reports no error bars or significance tests. Some evaluation formats, especially comprehension, supply the relevant information in context and therefore do not isolate knowledge stored in model weights.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3 and 4 report results at steps 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, and 30 across formats and retain/forget subsets. To stay within the row limit, this record includes step-30 forget-subset results for the seven listed formats and omits the other steps and retain-subset rows; the default step-0 values are noted where pertinent. Figures 2, 3, 18, and 19 provide plotted results but are not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Broad general capability (e.g. MMLU) is not measured; only TOFU retain-set knowledge is.
No relearning or fine-tuning after unlearning.
No activation ablation or internal analysis.
No jailbreaks, other languages, or adversarial prompt search. Only fixed format transformations, on the TOFU fictitious-author setting, with GA, KL and GD only.

missing.what: Retain-set rows (Q&A, Cloze, MCQA, comprehension) at step 30 for each method; needed to judge A's 'keeps general ability'.
Intermediate steps, especially Llama2 GD step 24: Q&A 0.4017 ≈ pretrained but Cloze 0.0154 near finetuned 0.0181. This is the strongest format gap.
MCQA 2-option forget results (Llama2 KL 0.7200 = pretrained; GA 0.5750).

record.verdict_notes: Uses a gap-closure reading: unlearned score's position between pretrained and finetuned. MCQA, analogy and comprehension often have tiny or negative finetuning headroom (finetuned at or below pretrained), so they cannot show recovery. The figure's step is unstated, and its text (Cloze 'much higher' than pretrained) matches step 24 better than step 30. No error bars; forget set is n=200. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that targeted accuracy reaches near chance while general ability is maintained, nor does it test whether simple attacks fail after that condition is achieved.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is used.
No activation-direction ablation or internal edit is tested, and no analysis establishes that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.

Tests alternative data formats for the same facts and comprehension prompts that supply facts in context. Does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or prompt-only reformulations without changing the task format.
No newer method is claimed or tested for resisting these attacks.
